node_definition.done_when: Read section 6 of a-finished-worktree-releases-without-a-force and the landed record's §4 first. reckon crew gc classifies a dirty worktree whose head is not an ancestor of the integration head by checking each commit beyond its merge base for a patch-equivalent on the integration head, with git cherry or git patch-id. A worktree whose every commit has an equivalent is released through the residue-preserving path that gc --apply already uses for dirty integrated worktrees. A worktree with any non-equivalent commit is kept, and gc's report names that commit's sha and subject. A worktree claimed by a live run is never touched. tests/test_gc_releases_squash_landed_worktrees.py covers, in a temporary repository and RECKON_HOME, an equivalent commit that releases with its residue saved, a non-equivalent commit that is kept and named, and a live-claimed worktree left untouched. Existing tests in tests/test_crew_gc.py and tests/test_finished_worktree_saves_residue.py keep passing; one that asserts an unintegrated dirty worktree is always kept is updated to the equivalence rule, and no case is deleted. No test touches a real worktree under ~/Code/.reckon-worktrees. Run `date -u` first and treat that instant as your start; your deadline is 60 minutes later. Write your manifest before starting any long command. Run both gate arms with pytest-xdist (-n 8 --timeout=300), never serially. Run the base arm, from a `git archive` extraction of your base under /tmp in a directory named for this run, and then the head arm, each in the foreground: a background command dies when your turn ends. Keep the gate to the test files that reach your change, tens of files rather than hundreds. Each arm uses its own basetemp outside any repository and writes to its own new log path, which it never overwrites. Each arm is recorded as JSON carrying completed true and a literal command with absolute paths and no angle-bracket placeholder. Each log names its revision on the first line and ends with a bare line reading EXIT= followed by the exit code. The head arm adds no failure id; any added id means status blocked, naming each id. ruff check and ruff format --check over the changed Python paths report no finding the base did not. Scratch goes under /tmp in a directory named for this run and is deleted before status complete. The turn ends once the manifest reads complete or blocked.
node_definition.goal: Release a dirty worktree whose commits all have patch-equivalents on main, as a-finished-worktree-releases-without-a-force §6 states.
